version_history.subject: [PATCH v3] mm: bypass swap readahead for zswap

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch bypasses swap readahead for zswap, an in-memory synchronous backend similar to zram. The current implementation of swap readahead can lead to pointless prefetching of pages, causing increased anon residency and page cache thrashing. By bypassing readahead for zswap, the patch aims to reduce this overhead and improve performance. Measurements show significant gains in build time, zswap-in/out rates, and reduced swap readahead hits. The patch reuses existing code and adds a new helper function to check if a swap entry is synchronous.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 1/2] mm/zswap: batch the writeback IO of consecutive entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the writeback I/O of zswap by batching consecutive entries into a single bio, reducing the number of I/O requests and improving performance. The patch introduces a new struct to share state between all entries written back in one LRU walk, allowing for more efficient use of I/O resources. The changes are based on measurements that show significant improvements in build time, write requests, pages per write request, iocost debt, and IO full pressure when batching is enabled.

series_items.subject: [PATCH 2/2] mm/zswap: plug the writeback IO of an LRU walk
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the writeback IO of an LRU walk in the zswap module by allowing the block layer to merge pending writes that cannot be batched together. This is achieved by plugging the LRU walk, which reduces the number of write requests and improves performance. The patch includes benchmark results showing a 6.8% reduction in write requests and a 21.6% reduction in iocost debt when running alone, and a 4.6% reduction in write requests and a 10.6% reduction in IO full pressure when running next to a sibling fio random writer.

patches_submitted.patch_summary: This patch series aims to improve the writeback IO performance of zswap by batching consecutive entries and allowing the block layer to merge them. review_comments.summary:

Reviewer noted that one potential issue in the patch is a refcount leak and suggested it be addressed separately.
review_comments.raw_body:

the PMD migration entry or split it with a partial zap? Although it
does not affect the correctness of the patch.

causing the folio to be not freed, since
split_huge_pmd_address(freeze=true) does not drop the folio refcount

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 12/30] mm/swap: allow duplicating a range of swap entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch allows duplicating a range of swap entries at once, rather than one slot at a time. This is necessary because the PMD swap entry fork path requires multiple slots to be duplicated simultaneously, and doing it one slot at a time would require acquiring and releasing the cluster lock multiple times. The patch introduces new functions `swap_dup_entries_direct` and `swap_retry_table_alloc_nr` that take an additional argument for the number of entries to duplicate, and renames existing functions to inline wrappers. The range of swap entries must be within one cluster, and attempting to duplicate a crossing range will result in an error.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 13/30] mm: handle PMD swap entries in fork path
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses an issue where PMD swap entries are not handled correctly in the fork path, leading to duplicated and unreferenced page table slots. The patch introduces a new function `copy_huge_non_present_pmd` that duplicates PMD swap entries by creating new references to the underlying pages and updating the mm counter accordingly. It also updates the `copy_huge_pmd` function to handle GFP_ATOMIC allocation failures for extend-tables, allowing the fork process to retry with GFP_KERNEL. The patch further refactors the code to move the mm counter update into each entry-type arm, improving consistency and accuracy in page table management.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 14/30] mm: zswap: reject high-order swap cache allocations backed by zswap
series_items.patch_summary: This patch rejects high-order swap cache allocations backed by zswap when the range of swap slots is split between zswap entries and the backing device. This prevents a disk read from returning stale or zero data for every slot owned by zswap. The check is performed after the folio is in the swap cache, ensuring that the answer is stable. If a high-order allocation over such a range is attempted, an error is returned. The patch also exports the zswap_is_present() function for use by PMD-order swap-in users.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 15/30] mm: swap in PMD swap entries as whole THPs during swapoff
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the behavior of the swapoff operation to handle PMD (Page Map Directory) swap entries as whole THPs (Transparent Huge Pages). The existing implementation would only consider PTEs, leading to incomplete swapoff operations. The patch introduces a new function `swap_pmd_cache_lookup` to classify PMD swap entries and map them back in as one THP, preserving soft-dirty, exclusive, and UFFD state. If the PMD entry is split or has per-page zswap state, it falls back to PTE handling.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 16/30] fs/proc: account PMD swap entries in smaps
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the smaps functionality in the Linux kernel to correctly account for PMD swap entries. It introduces a new function, smaps_account_swap(), which is called when a swapped-out THP is encountered. This function calculates the correct Swap and SwapPss values based on the swap reference counts of each slot in the PMD entry. The patch also updates the smaps_pte_entry() and smaps_pmd_entry() functions to use this new function, ensuring that device-private PMD entries are treated as fake-present and allowing for accurate PSS and private/shared accounting.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 17/30] mm: handle soft-dirty and uffd-wp on PMD swap entries
series_items.patch_summary: This patch updates the Linux kernel to correctly handle soft-dirty and uffd-wp flags on PMD swap entries, ensuring that these flags are properly updated during page table operations. The changes affect several functions in fs/proc/task_mmu.c and mm/huge_memory.c, where the code now checks for both migration and swap entries when updating these flags. This patch addresses a problem where clearing soft-dirty would skip swapped-out THPs, UFFDIO_WRITEPROTECT would not arm it, and mremap would not mark the destination correctly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 18/30] mm/hmm: fault PMD swap entries on demand
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the handling of absent PMD entries in the Linux kernel's Heterogeneous Memory Management (HMM) module. When a swapped-out huge page is encountered, it will no longer be reported as an error, but instead treated like a PTE swap entry and recorded as such when a fault occurs. This change ensures that memory that needs to be paged in is properly identified and handled.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 19/30] mm: free PMD swap entries in zap_huge_pmd()
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the zap_huge_pmd() function to handle PMD swap entries before attempting to access a folio. It checks if the cleared PMD is a swap entry and, if so, frees the associated swap slots and updates the memory management counters accordingly.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 20/30] mm/madvise: free PMD swap entries with MADV_FREE
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the Linux kernel's memory management to free PMD swap entries when using the MADV_FREE advisory. Currently, madvise_free_pte_range() only frees present THP pages and ignores swapped-out pages. The patch introduces a new approach where it checks if the entire PMD is covered by the advice and, if so, frees all its slots at once. Otherwise, it splits the range into smaller sub-ranges that can be handled by the PTE path. This change ensures that MADV_FREE over a swapped-out THP silently does nothing, which was the previous behavior.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 21/30] mm/madvise: skip PMD swap entries for MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT
series_items.patch_summary: This patch optimizes the handling of PMD swap entries for MADV_COLD and MADV_PAGEOUT operations in the Linux kernel's mm/madvise module. It skips unnecessary processing when a swapped-out huge page (THP) has no resident folio to deactivate or reclaim, preventing potential issues with migration or device-private entries. The patch introduces a check for PMD swap entries before attempting to map PTE tables, ensuring efficient and correct handling of these operations.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 22/30] mm/madvise: keep PMD swap entries whole for MADV_GUARD_INSTALL/REMOVE
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the MADV_GUARD_INSTALL and REMOVE callbacks in the Linux kernel to handle PMD swap entries correctly. Currently, these callbacks test for huge pages using pmd_trans_huge(), but this is false for PMD swap entries, leading to incorrect behavior when trying to install or remove guard pages. The patch adds a check for PMD swap entries using pmd_is_swap_entry() and returns immediately if the entry is swapped out, preventing unnecessary splitting of the page table.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 23/30] mm/mincore: report PMD swap-cache residency
series_items.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the mincore function where it incorrectly reports huge PMD pages as resident when they are actually swapped out. The patch introduces a new function, mincore_pmd_swap, which looks up the swap cache for PMD-sized folios and returns residency information for each page within that range. If the PMD-sized folio was split while its entry remained in the swap cache, the function falls back to looking up each covered slot individually. The patch also adds a new check to handle PMD swap entries without CONFIG_THP_SWAP enabled.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 24/30] mm/khugepaged: treat PMD swap entries as mapped THPs
series_items.patch_summary: This patch modifies the khugepaged code to treat PMD swap entries as mapped THPs, allowing them to be handled similarly to present huge PMDs. This change affects how MADV_COLLAPSE handles swapped-out THPs, ensuring that they are still collapsed into a single THP on first touch. The approach taken is to add a new condition in the check_pmd_state function to return SCAN_PMD_MAPPED for PMD swap entries.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 25/30] mm: handle PMD swap entries in MADV_WILLNEED
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves handling of PMD swap entries in MADV_WILLNEED operations by prefetching the whole range as one PMD-order folio instead of walking PTEs individually. This approach avoids issues with order-0 readahead and subsequent faults, and ensures that the eventual fault still takes do_huge_pmd_swap_page(). The patch also checks the THP policy before reading at PMD order to prevent handing do_swap_page() a PMD-sized folio to map with PTEs. If the prefetch fails or if the PMD is split, the patch falls back to the PTE path, which can still read the slots at order 0.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 26/30] mm: handle PMD swap entries in UFFDIO_MOVE
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds support for moving PMD-level swap entries in UFFDIO_MOVE operations. It introduces a new function, move_swap_pmd(), which handles the movement of these entries under both PMD locks. The function propagates soft-dirty bits and arms the UFFD marker for an RWP-registered destination. It also revalidates the folio's association with the swap entry and updates the anon rmap metadata. The patch rejects a PMD swap entry at the destination with -EEXIST, as it is not a hole and does not resolve on its own. This patch addresses a problem where aligned UFFDIO_MOVE operations over swapped-out THPs fail due to the lack of support for PMD-level swap entries.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 27/30] mm: don't PTE-batch a swap-in over a hardware-poisoned subpage
series_items.patch_summary: This patch prevents the PTE-batching mechanism from mapping a swap-in over a hardware-poisoned subpage, which could lead to undetected faults. The problem arises because the batching path doesn't check for poisoned subpages individually, allowing a faulting page to be mapped even if one of its subpages is poisoned. To fix this, the patch adds a check to ensure that each subpage is tested separately before mapping the folio, using the `folio_has_hwpoisoned_subpage` function to detect poisoned subpages.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 28/30] mm: handle PMD swap entry faults on swap-in
series_items.patch_summary: This patch addresses a problem where PMD (Page Map Directory) swap entries would fault indefinitely when swapped out, causing a VM_FAULT_OOM error. The solution is to split the PMD entry into individual PTEs and return 0, allowing the retry to land in do_swap_page(). This approach ensures that transient allocation failures do not become permanent errors. Additionally, the patch handles various edge cases, such as dropping folios from the swap cache when necessary, refusing to map poisoned subpages, and calling wp_huge_pmd() for write faults on read-only PMDs.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 29/30] mm: install PMD swap entries on swap-out
series_items.patch_summary: This patch improves the handling of PMD-mapped anonymous huge pages (THPs) during swap-out operations. When a THP is swapped out, it was previously split into smaller mappings, which caused performance issues and unnecessary overhead. This patch introduces a new approach where a single PMD-level swap entry is installed for each contiguous run of slots in the swap cache, eliminating the need for splitting and reducing the number of faults during swap-in. The patch also updates various kernel components to support this new behavior, including the huge memory management code, rmap, vmscan, and vmstat.

series_items.subject: [PATCH v8 30/30] selftests/mm: add PMD swap entry tests
series_items.patch_summary: This patch adds tests for PMD (Page Map Directory) swap entries to the Linux kernel's selftest suite. The tests verify that PMD-mapped huge pages are correctly swapped out and in, including edge cases such as asynchronous devices and zswap enabled systems. The patch also includes a new /proc/vmstat field reader and registers the pmd_swap test with the default runner. The tests cover various scenarios, including fork, write, munmap, mprotect, and swapoff, to ensure that PMD swap entries are handled correctly.

On 10/2/26 11:52, Usama Arif wrote:
> When reclaim swaps out a PMD-mapped anonymous THP today, the PMD is
> split into HPAGE_PMD_NR PTE-level swap entries via TTU_SPLIT_HUGE_PMD
> before unmap.  This series introduces a PMD-level swap entry so the
> huge mapping can survive the swap round-trip and do_huge_pmd_swap_page()
> can restore the PMD mapping directly on swap-in, without waiting for
> khugepaged to collapse the range later.
> 
> The PMD swap entry is a compact page-table encoding for HPAGE_PMD_NR
> consecutive swap slots.  swap_map accounting remains per-slot and is
> unchanged.  Importantly, a PMD swap entry does not promise that the swap
> cache always contains one PMD-sized folio.  While the cache is empty or
> contains one PMD-sized folio, PMD-level handling can proceed.  Once the
> cache has split/per-slot state, users either inspect the individual
> slots directly (mincore) or split the PMD swap entry and retry through
> the PTE path (fault, swapoff, MADV_WILLNEED, UFFDIO_MOVE).  MADV_FREE
> does not consult the cache at all: it frees a whole PMD swap entry in
> place and only splits when the advised range covers part of the PMD.
> Likewise, if any slot is still backed by zswap's per-page
> store, PMD-order swap-in consumers split and let the PTE path load the
> range page by page; an all-on-disk range can still be read back as one
> PMD-sized folio.
> 
> The series is ordered so every consumer can handle PMD swap entries
> before the swap-out producer starts installing them.  The swap-out patch
> is the last functional change.
> 
> Performance:
> 
>   Measured with vm-scalability's case-swap-w-seq benchmark [1].  Four
>   pinned workers repeatedly write a 6 GiB anonymous working set on a
>   4 vCPU / 4 GiB guest, forcing the set out to swap and back in.  Swap
>   is an 8 GiB NOCOW raw virtio device (cache=none, aio=native), zswap is
>   disabled, and THP enabled/defrag are both "always".  The numbers below
>   are medians of five interleaved runs per kernel after one warm-up run:
> 
>   Metric                          Baseline     Patched      Change
>   Aggregate throughput            584.3 MiB/s  2408.9 MiB/s +312.2% (4.12x)
>   Elapsed time                    85.43 s      20.72 s      -75.7%
>   Major faults                    1,814,699    228,466      -87.4%
>   Swap I/O rate                   1.02 GiB/s   4.10 GiB/s   +303.9%
> 
>   This is a swap-intensive synthetic workload, so it mostly demonstrates
>   the reduction in swap-fault and page-table overhead from preserving
>   PMD mappings.  I don't want to use sythetic workloads to show benefits
>   of the series. IMHO, the main advantage comes from long-running
>   workloads I expect the bigger win to come from fewer TLB misses,
>   less khugepaged work, and less kernel churn from larger folios, although
>   I have not found a benchmark that captures that well.  PMD swap entries
>   also move us closer to eliminating page-table deposits for anonymous THPs,
>   which would provide memory savings.
>

> 
>   Because the swap-out producer is the last functional patch, the
>   consumer code added by the patches before it is unreachable at the

On 2 Oct 2026, at 10:28, David Hildenbrand (Arm) wrote:

> On 10/2/26 11:52, Usama Arif wrote:
>> When reclaim swaps out a PMD-mapped anonymous THP today, the PMD is
>> split into HPAGE_PMD_NR PTE-level swap entries via TTU_SPLIT_HUGE_PMD
>> before unmap.  This series introduces a PMD-level swap entry so the
>> huge mapping can survive the swap round-trip and do_huge_pmd_swap_page()
>> can restore the PMD mapping directly on swap-in, without waiting for
>> khugepaged to collapse the range later.
>>
>> The PMD swap entry is a compact page-table encoding for HPAGE_PMD_NR
>> consecutive swap slots.  swap_map accounting remains per-slot and is
>> unchanged.  Importantly, a PMD swap entry does not promise that the swap
>> cache always contains one PMD-sized folio.  While the cache is empty or
>> contains one PMD-sized folio, PMD-level handling can proceed.  Once the
>> cache has split/per-slot state, users either inspect the individual
>> slots directly (mincore) or split the PMD swap entry and retry through
>> the PTE path (fault, swapoff, MADV_WILLNEED, UFFDIO_MOVE).  MADV_FREE
>> does not consult the cache at all: it frees a whole PMD swap entry in
>> place and only splits when the advised range covers part of the PMD.
>> Likewise, if any slot is still backed by zswap's per-page
>> store, PMD-order swap-in consumers split and let the PTE path load the
>> range page by page; an all-on-disk range can still be read back as one
>> PMD-sized folio.
>>
>> The series is ordered so every consumer can handle PMD swap entries
>> before the swap-out producer starts installing them.  The swap-out patch
>> is the last functional change.
>>

On 10/2/26 5:52 AM, Usama Arif wrote:
> When reclaim swaps out a PMD-mapped anonymous THP today, the PMD is
> split into HPAGE_PMD_NR PTE-level swap entries via TTU_SPLIT_HUGE_PMD
> before unmap.  This series introduces a PMD-level swap entry so the
> huge mapping can survive the swap round-trip and do_huge_pmd_swap_page()
> can restore the PMD mapping directly on swap-in, without waiting for
> khugepaged to collapse the range later.
> 
> The PMD swap entry is a compact page-table encoding for HPAGE_PMD_NR
> consecutive swap slots.  swap_map accounting remains per-slot and is
> unchanged.  Importantly, a PMD swap entry does not promise that the swap
> cache always contains one PMD-sized folio.  While the cache is empty or
> contains one PMD-sized folio, PMD-level handling can proceed.  Once the
> cache has split/per-slot state, users either inspect the individual
> slots directly (mincore) or split the PMD swap entry and retry through
> the PTE path (fault, swapoff, MADV_WILLNEED, UFFDIO_MOVE).  MADV_FREE
> does not consult the cache at all: it frees a whole PMD swap entry in
> place and only splits when the advised range covers part of the PMD.
> Likewise, if any slot is still backed by zswap's per-page
> store, PMD-order swap-in consumers split and let the PTE path load the
> range page by page; an all-on-disk range can still be read back as one
> PMD-sized folio.
> 
> The series is ordered so every consumer can handle PMD swap entries
> before the swap-out producer starts installing them.  The swap-out patch
> is the last functional change.
> 
> Performance:
> 
>    Measured with vm-scalability's case-swap-w-seq benchmark [1].  Four
>    pinned workers repeatedly write a 6 GiB anonymous working set on a
>    4 vCPU / 4 GiB guest, forcing the set out to swap and back in.  Swap
>    is an 8 GiB NOCOW raw virtio device (cache=none, aio=native), zswap is
>    disabled, and THP enabled/defrag are both "always".  The numbers below
>    are medians of five interleaved runs per kernel after one warm-up run:
> 
>    Metric                          Baseline     Patched      Change
>    Aggregate throughput            584.3 MiB/s  2408.9 MiB/s +312.2% (4.12x)
>    Elapsed time                    85.43 s      20.72 s      -75.7%
>    Major faults                    1,814,699    228,466      -87.4%
>    Swap I/O rate                   1.02 GiB/s   4.10 GiB/s   +303.9%
> 
>    This is a swap-intensive synthetic workload, so it mostly demonstrates
>    the reduction in swap-fault and page-table overhead from preserving
>    PMD mappings.  I don't want to use sythetic workloads to show benefits
>    of the series. IMHO, the main advantage comes from long-running
>    workloads I expect the bigger win to come from fewer TLB misses,
>    less khugepaged work, and less kernel churn from larger folios, although
>    I have not found a benchmark that captures that well.  PMD swap entries
>    also move us closer to eliminating page-table deposits for anonymous THPs,
>    which would provide memory savings.
> 
> Sashiko reviews on intermediate patches:
> 
>    Because the swap-out producer is the last functional patch, the
>    consumer code added by the patches before it is unreachable at the
>    point it is introduced.  Every previous sashiko review has reported
>    that code as broken on the basis of a state it cannot yet be in; the
>    series is ordered this way deliberately.  See [2].
> 
> Notes on zswap:
> 
>    Native PMD-order zswap load/store is intentionally left for a follow-up.
>    Alexandre Ghiti is currently working on this.
>    This series can still preserve PMD swap entries while zswap is enabled:
>    zswap stores the THP as order-0 entries, and PMD-order swap-in
>    consumers split any range that has zswap entries before reading it.  If
>    zswap has written the whole range back to disk, or the swap cache still
>    contains one PMD-sized folio, PMD-level handling can proceed.
> 
> Testing:
> 
>    The 17 pmd_swap selftests pass on x86_64 with zswap both disabled and
>    enabled.  PMD_SWAP_DEVICE was the sole active swap device, so the
>    swapoff test ran in both configurations.  Note that with zswap enabled
>    the range may legitimately come back through the PTE fallback, so those
>    runs skip the PMD-restoration assertions and say so in the log; the
>    zswap-disabled run is the one that proves PMD restoration.
> 
>    hmm-tests was run with CONFIG_DEBUG_VM=y and panic_on_warn=1, both on
>    this series and on the base commit: identical results either way
>    (pass:35 fail:3 skip:40).  The three failures are O_TMPFILE on the
>    test VM's 9p /tmp, not kernel behaviour, and the THP paths
>    (migrate_anon_huge_*, migrate_partial_unmap_fault,
>    benchmark_thp_migration) pass.
